decisions.quality_evidence: iTermGraphEncoder makes scalar versus child-graph encoding, identity, generation, append-only rollback, conditional fields, encryption selection, and record construction explicit; iTermGraphDeltaEncoder and iTermGraphDatabase make previous-revision comparison, transactional writes, row identifiers, root publication, loading, integrity checks, garbage collection, bounded recovery, and deep-copy isolation visible; names preserve graph and restoration vocabulary; modern database, delta, recovery, and restoration suites exercise persistence, changes, cycles, failures, repair, identities, and round trips; project guides orient invariants; the application-state-to-restored-graph trace is complete; and the exact public pin, GPL-2.0-or-later terms in COPYING, maintained production path, and regression coverage satisfy all eight quality dimensions.

learning_path.goal: Understand how iTerm2 encodes a restorable object graph, persists only graph changes transactionally in SQLite, and recovers a consistent baseline after save or database failure.
learning_path.trace: Start with graph-database initialization and load, follow state encoding into scalar and child records, stable identifiers and generations, delta comparison against the prior revision, table transformation and one SQLite transaction, row-id publication and garbage collection; then force a failed save through bounded recovery, fresh full encoding, deep-copy isolation and integrity assertions before closing persistence, delta, corruption, rollback, and recovery behavior in the modern suites.

signals: Objective-C graph-encodable protocols, blocks, categories, and typed records
Objective-C and Swift interoperability around SQLite and restoration models
custom coder adaptation, cyclic-object handling, deep copy, and asynchronous thread confinement
language_technique.reason: Advanced Objective-C and interoperability techniques recur across encoding, persistence, and recovery.

signals: cyclic graph identity, generations, prior revision, and delta propagation
transactional save, root publication, garbage collection, load, and asynchronous ownership
failed-save recovery, deep-copy isolation, row-id repair, retries, and integrity assertions
behavioral_reasoning.reason: Expert nonlocal graph, persistence, lifecycle, failure, and recovery reasoning is pervasive.

signals: delta encoder, record model, relational transformer, SQLite wrapper, and database coordinator
threading, encryption, filesystem, and modern recovery-test boundaries
design_span.reason: Several major subsystems and external boundaries cooperate in one bounded state-restoration slice.

signals: object identity, cycles, generations, row IDs, graph reachability, and previous revisions must remain coherent
transactions, publication, rollback, garbage collection, failed-save recovery, and retries must never expose a corrupt baseline
application compatibility, encryption, SQLite durability, asynchronous ordering, performance, and restoration fidelity interact
constraint_burden.reason: Several system-wide integrity, durability, failure-recovery, security, compatibility, and performance guarantees interact.

decisions.evidence: Retain: both gates pass and 4/5/4/5 sums to 18, whose mean of 4.5 rounds half up to Level 5; behavioral reasoning and constraint burden both score 5, satisfying the Level 5 guard, and iTerm2 ranks first of two qualified Objective-C Level 5 paths.
decisions.reconsider: Reconsider if graph identity, delta, transaction, row-id, recovery, restoration, test, GPL-2.0-or-later licensing, maintenance, or comparative Objective-C Level 5 clarity materially changes.

second_review.notes: Independent exact-pin inspection confirmed both gate passes, replacement of the catalog's terminal-wide path with the bounded state-restoration graph database, 4/5/4/5 scores, Level 5 rank 1, GPL-2.0-or-later evidence in COPYING, and retention.

domain_context: A notification center registers observers by optional notification name and object and synchronously dispatches matching notifications; nil names or objects act as wildcards.
coding_relevance.evidence: That short framework primer is subordinate to transferable expert library engineering in Objective-C runtime dispatch, weak observer identity, selector and block APIs, wildcard indexing, custom allocation, striped and recursive locking, snapshotting before callbacks, reentrant add and remove, deallocation races, queued delivery, exception safety, compatibility, and concurrency tests.

decisions.quality_evidence: NSNotificationCenter makes wildcard, name, object, receiver, selector, and block registrations explicit; custom observation allocation and hash tables keep hot-path ownership visible; striped locks, recursive bookkeeping, snapshots and deferred release protect reentrant posting and removal; public method names mirror Foundation contracts; basic, general, and dynamic tests cover construction, equality, selectors, blocks, wildcard combinations, duplicate registrations, removal scopes, mutation while posting, nested posts, lifetime, threading, and compatibility; headers and README orient semantics; the registration-to-callback trace is complete; and the exact public pin, LGPL-2.0-or-later source plus GPL-2.0-only test evidence in COPYING.LIB and COPYING, mature implementation, and focused tests satisfy all eight quality dimensions.

learning_path.goal: Understand how GNUstep implements a reentrant, thread-safe Foundation-compatible notification center with exact wildcard, observer-lifetime, selector, and block-delivery semantics.
learning_path.trace: Start with the observation record and notification tables, follow addObserver into wildcard, name, object, receiver and selector indexes under recursive and striped locks, then trace postNotification through matching-list snapshots, unlock-before-callback delivery, selector or queued block invocation, reentrant mutation, exception and cleanup paths; finish with scoped and total removal, observer lifetime, nested posting, wildcard, mutation, and threading contracts in the three focused suites.

signals: manual Objective-C runtime selector dispatch and weak observer identity
custom observation arenas, C structs, intrusive lists, hash tables, and cached classes
blocks, NSOperation queue delivery, pthread-backed recursive and striped synchronization
language_technique.reason: Multiple expert Objective-C runtime, ownership, data-structure, callback, and synchronization mechanisms interact pervasively.

signals: wildcard, name, object, observer, selector, and block matching across several indexes
snapshot, unlock, callback, reentrant add or remove, nested post, and deferred-release lifecycle
concurrent registration, removal, posting, observer deallocation, exceptions, and queued delivery
behavioral_reasoning.reason: Expert nonlocal identity, matching, event-order, reentrancy, ownership, and concurrency reasoning is pervasive.

signals: public Foundation-compatible notification and center APIs
internal tables, observation allocator, locks, selector and block delivery
design_span.reason: Several meaningful runtime-library units cooperate, while the path remains one bounded Foundation subsystem.

signals: wildcard matching, duplicate registration, scoped removal, callback order, and Foundation compatibility must remain exact
reentrant mutation, nested posting, observer deallocation, exceptions, queue delivery, and concurrent access must never corrupt tables or message dead observers
ownership modes, runtime variants, historical API behavior, hot-path performance, portability, and binary compatibility interact
constraint_burden.reason: Several system-wide correctness, lifetime, concurrency, reentrancy, compatibility, portability, and performance guarantees interact.

decisions.evidence: Retain: both gates pass and 5/5/3/5 sums to 18, whose mean of 4.5 rounds half up to Level 5; three dimensions score 5, satisfying the Level 5 guard, and GNUstep Base's notification center ranks second of two qualified Objective-C Level 5 paths.
decisions.reconsider: Reconsider if observer identity, wildcard matching, callback order, reentrancy, lifetime, concurrency, compatibility, tests, compound LGPL-2.0-or-later and GPL-2.0-only evidence, or comparative Objective-C Level 5 clarity materially changes.

second_review.notes: Independent exact-pin inspection confirmed both gate passes, replacement of the catalog's framework-wide path with the bounded notification-center implementation and three direct suites, 5/5/3/5 scores, Level 5 rank 2, LGPL-2.0-or-later source plus GPL-2.0-only test licensing, and retention.
